content: The contents of one bottle (118 mL) should be administered rectally as a single dose. This product may also be used following barium studies. The patient should lie on their left side with the right knee bent. To administer, gently insert the enema tip into the rectum using a slight side-to-side motion, directing the tip toward the navel. To facilitate insertion, the patient can bear down as if having a bowel movement to relax the anal muscles. Do not force the enema tip into the rectum. Squeeze the bottle to deliver all its contents, then remove the enema tip. The enema should be retained as per the doctor’s instructions. If the stool remains hard or not lubricated, a cleansing enema may be required. For children under 1 year of age, safety and efficacy have not been established. For children aged 2 to 12 years, administer half a bottle (59 mL) rectally as a single dose. For individuals over 12 years of age, the dosage is the same as for adults: the contents of one bottle (118 mL) rectally as a single dose. The administration technique remains the same: the patient should lie on their left side with the right knee bent, gently insert the enema tip toward the navel, and avoid forcing the tip. Squeeze the bottle to deliver the appropriate dose, remove the tip, and retain the enema as instructed by a healthcare provider. Potential side effects include anal seepage, pruritus ani (itching around the anus), perianal discomfort, and hypersensitivity reactions. This product should not be used by patients with colostomy, ileostomy, appendicitis, ulcerative colitis, or diverticulitis. It is also contraindicated in children under 13 years of age, bedridden patients, and those currently taking stool softeners or laxatives. This product is for rectal use only. Excessive use may lead to complications such as electrolyte imbalance, steatorrhea (fatty stools), osteomalacia (softening of bones), diarrhea, and cathartic colon (colon damage due to laxative overuse). Consult a healthcare professional if you have already used a laxative for more than three days, are experiencing abdominal pain, nausea, or vomiting, or have had sudden changes in bowel habits that persist for more than two weeks. This product should only be used at bedtime and should not be administered to infants unless directed by a physician. Discontinue use and seek medical advice if you experience rectal bleeding or fail to have a bowel movement within 30 minutes of enema use. Keep this product out of the reach of children. If swallowed, seek medical help or contact a Poison Control Center immediately at 800-222-1222. For pregnant women, this product is generally considered safe. Controlled studies in pregnant women have shown no evidence of fetal risk. However, it is always advisable to consult a healthcare professional before use.
